rollback.cli: # fill in: keep the flag list from gcloud sql instances describe <instance> --project=<project> --format='json(settings.databaseFlags)' before the change; patching the instance with that list restores it

cli: # fill in: gcloud sql instances describe <instance> --project=<project> --format='json(settings.databaseFlags)', then run gcloud sql instances patch <instance> --project=<project> with every current flag plus shared_buffers=524288
notes: Cloud SQL restarts the instance to apply this flag: an outage of about a minute.
Cloud SQL supports a subset of PostgreSQL settings as flags; gcloud rejects an unsupported one without changing the instance.
blockers: The instance's current database flags are unknown (no credentials): --database-flags replaces every flag, so pg_sage gives a fill-in template instead of a command. Read the existing flags (gcloud sql instances describe) and include them all.
auto_apply_withheld: pg_sage never applies provider parameter changes in this release: an operator runs the command (most need a reboot, an outage) and pg_sage verifies the running value afterwards
